Run day-to-day finance operations on the payables side: accounts payable, payment runs, and a clean, on-time procure-to-pay process
Support our outgoing invoicing process, from creating and issuing customer invoices through to tracking receivables and incoming payments
Support the monthly closing and prepare our financial investor reporting, working closely with the Head of Finance and our external accountants
Track budgets and actuals across cost centers and flag deviations early
Act as the internal counterpart to our external accountants and tax advisor on year-end audits and tax filings
Help level up our finance stack and processes, from DATEV workflows to spend-management and finance tooling. You won't just run processes, you'll design your own
Own non-tech procurement, from sourcing and ordering through to vendor and contract management
Manage employee travel arrangements and expense reporting
Take on general company administration that keeps the team running, from office-related purchasing to ad hoc operational tasks
What You Bring
1 to 2 years of experience in finance and/or operations, ideally in a startup or fast-paced environment. Strong, relevant internship experience counts too if you're a fast learner
Fluent German and English, German at C1 level or above. This is a hard requirement: our finance and administrative processes run in a German-language context (DATEV, tax advisors, audits, vendor and authority communication)
A solid grasp of accounting fundamentals and a working understanding of how P&L, balance sheet, and cash flow connect. Bookkeeping is handled externally, but you know what's happening behind the numbers
Hands-on exposure to procure-to-pay processes and purchasing, ideally including hardware
Familiarity with DATEV and comfort with spend-management or finance tools
A strong numerical sense and confident Excel skills
A structured, detail-oriented way of working paired with a proactive, ownership-driven mindset. You identify what needs to happen next and take it on
You communicate openly, enjoy working in an international team, and are eager to grow alongside it
Not ticking every box? That's okay. One exception to the above: German at C1 level or above is required for this role.
If this role excites you and you bring most of what we've described, we want to hear from you.

Mission & Technical Challenge:
At Omegga, you work on problems that are both technically demanding and globally relevant. We build deep-tech solutions with real-world impact, pushing the boundaries of what's currently possible.

Moving to Munich? We help you find an apartment in the Werksviertel within walking distance of the office. We connect you with the right contacts and take the stress out of apartment hunting.

Ownership:
VSOPs (Virtual Stock Options) so you share in the value you help create.
Time Off:
28 vacation days per year, plus December 24th and 31st off.

Monthly meal budget for whatever keeps you going, from quick lunches to proper team dinners
Monthly perks budget to spend where it actually matters to you: fitness, mobility, or the occasional "I earned this" purchase

We promote environmental health through legal and data-driven program support, using innovative methods to track environmental determinants of health with a focus on New Yorkers disproportionately impacted by environmental risk. We share data and research findings to encourage evidence-based decision-making, and partner with communities in community science and outreach to address stakeholder concerns and empower residents. The Bureau of Environmental Science and Policy (BESP) seeks to hire a lawyer to serve as Executive Director of the Environmental Health Legal team (EH Legal). BESP's mission is to ground Health Department programs and policy in science and law to support a healthy and equitable natural, and occupational environment for all New Yorkers. We promote environmental health through legal and data-driven program support, using innovative methods to track environmental determinants of health with a focus on New Yorkers disproportionately impacted by environmental risk. EH Legal supports the diverse legal needs of the Division's regulatory, enforcement and policy initiatives, collaborating with division leadership and the agency's Office of General Counsel (OGC). Reporting to the Assistant Commissioner, the Executive Director will assume oversight responsibility for multiple legal and policy projects and team supervision, while operating with a wide degree of independence and autonomy. The team supports the work of the Division by developing regulations; analyzing legislative proposals; advising inspectional programs regarding enforcement actions; prosecuting civil summonses at administrative hearings at the Office of Administrative Hearings and Tribunals (OATH); and advising programs on new initiatives. We seek a lawyer dedicated to creative use of the law to protect and promote the health of all New Yorkers, a leader who inspires innovative policy ideas, and a manager who equally values their team and the work. description:
About us

We love pets - which is why we're on a mission to make the world a better place for pets and their parents. We offer pet insurance policies with generous pet health benefits that are designed with their needs in mind. We've helped half a million pets stay happy and healthy since 2017 - and many more customers throughout the world are joining us every day. Our company is respectful, fun-loving and passionate about pets and their wellbeing. Throughout our business you'll meet people who think differently, aim for impact, and love to try new things. Want to join our pack? Join us. Love every moment. Love ManyPets.
A day in the life

As a Platform Engineer, you will join our platform squad. We build and maintain the AWS infrastructure, deployment pipelines, tooling and engineering standards that every other squad at ManyPets depends on.

This role has a security focus. Much of your first year will be spent building the tooling that lets us demonstrate our security controls are working: automated compliance checks, reporting, and evidence collection to support our ISO 27001 commitments. Alongside that you will help us tighten access controls across our cloud estate, and take on ownership of the edge and network security tooling that protects our services.

You will also work closely with our Head of Security as we build out a dedicated security capability at ManyPets.

Our environment is fast-paced and highly collaborative. You will work closely with your teammates using pair or mob programming, participating in regular workshops and planning sessions, primarily over Zoom, with occasional in-person collaboration.

We embrace modern development practices:

All our services are cloud-hosted on AWS, using serverless and event-driven architectures for scalability and resilience.

We use a fully automated deployment pipeline, allowing you to release to production within minutes, multiple times per day.

We define our infrastructure as code, and we emphasise observability, testing and secure-by-design principles from the start.

As a squad we own our work end-to-end, including development, maintenance and support. You will play a key role in ensuring the reliability and quality of what we provide to the rest of engineering, and contribute to a culture of rapid learning and continuous improvement.

Your responsibilities

ü Build and maintain secure platform foundations

Design, build and maintain the shared cloud infrastructure, tooling and deployment pipelines that other squads rely on.

Define infrastructure as code so our environments are consistent, repeatable and reviewable.

Make secure configuration the default, so squads get it without having to ask for it.

Maintain the edge and network security tooling that protects our services.

Share in the day-to-day operational ownership of the platform, responding to requests and issues raised by other squads.

ü Make our security controls provable

Build automated checks that continuously test our cloud estate against our security and compliance requirements.

Automate the collection and reporting of evidence for ISO 27001, replacing manual effort.

Surface and report on gaps, drift and findings so they can be prioritised and resolved.

Work with our Head of Security to turn written policy into controls that are enforced by tooling.

ü Strengthen access and identity controls

Review and tighten access across our cloud accounts, working towards least privilege.

Improve how we manage secrets, credentials and machine identities.

Make access changes auditable, and straightforward for engineers to request and for us to review.

ü Extend our platform standards beyond AWS

Help us apply the standards, tooling and controls we have built in AWS to our Google Cloud estate.

Work with the teams who use Google Cloud to understand their needs and where the gaps are.

ü Team collaboration

Work closely with other squad members and stakeholders to align on goals and solutions.

Support engineers across other squads who use our platform, and take their feedback seriously.

Proactively build shared understanding across the team through pairing, discussions, and reviews.

Document your work clearly to support knowledge sharing and future maintenance.

ü Self development

Take ownership of your learning journey and technical development plan.

Approach challenges with curiosity and a growth mindset.

Learn from your peers and actively seek feedback and mentorship.

Your skills and experience

We are looking for someone with:

Commercial experience building and maintaining cloud infrastructure on a major cloud provider (AWS, Google Cloud or Azure).

Hands-on experience defining infrastructure as code, using CDK, Terraform or similar.

Experience building and maintaining continuous integration and deployment pipelines.

A good working understanding of cloud security fundamentals, including identity and access management, secrets management, network controls and encryption.

Proficiency in at least one scripting language, ideally Python.

Comfort working in a regulated environment. We are FCA regulated and take our ISO 27001 commitments seriously.

We would also like to see at least one of the following. You do not need both, and we will support you to build the other:

A security specialism, such as cloud security posture management, security tooling, threat modelling or compliance automation.

Experience across more than one cloud provider, ideally both AWS and Google Cloud.

The interview process

This position has a four-stage interview process, which will be held via Zoom.

Stage 1 - an initial conversation with a member of our Talent team.

Stage 2 - an informal meeting with the hiring manager for about 45 minutes. We will explain more about the role and explore how your experience matches up with what we need.

Stage 3 - a longer interview, up to an hour, with the hiring manager and two engineers from the team. We will ask some competency questions and work through a technical scenario together. There is no take-home exercise.

Stage 4 - an informal conversation with our Head of Security.

About the team

The EPD ("Engineering, Product and Design") team operates with a squad system and Agile ways of working within quarterly terms - and we really enjoy working collaboratively. We hold regular 'Hack Weeks' to look at products and address problems relating to the business, and we get the chance to highlight and work on things we're interested in and feel passionately about.

Our tech stack

We are on a mission to become the best we can be, constantly challenging ourselves to achieve and learn. You will be supported to learn new technology – both in breadth and depth - and encouraged to challenge our ways of thinking with new and innovative ideas.

Our "north star" is to become an elite performer as defined by the 4 key DORA metrics. To drive towards elite status, we apply and continually inspect and adapt the best Agile frameworks and practices inspired by DevOps, SRE, Scrum, XP and Lean. We are a highly collaborative environment and regularly practice Mob and Pair based programming which we believe improve our quality of delivery and share understanding.

We take our operational performance, security, and reliability as seriously as our quality and development practices. We are cloud hosted and highly automated, primarily on AWS with some critical services running on Google Cloud.

Some specific technologies we use include: AWS | Google Cloud | Python | CDK | GitHub Actions | MongoDB | Aikido | Cloudflare
Salary range:
£55,000
—
£65,000 GBP
Ways of working

On a typical day you'll be working from a laptop with a screen, mouse, keyboard, and headset. You'll be meeting your colleagues on Zoom and keeping in touch regularly via email and Slack too – we'd expect you to be using your computer for around seven hours a day. We'd ask that you have a distraction-free work area and a reliable internet connection with a speed of 25Mbps so you can work effectively. We'll make sure you have the right home set-up that supports you in the role by providing best-in-class technology, money towards a desk, and vision support.

Inclusion at ManyPets

We promise to give you the same opportunities as everyone else and we won't discriminate against you at any point in the process. Our Opportunity

Over the past three years, Predium has built the leading real estate intelligence platform for ESG and value management in the DACH region - with the strongest names in the industry as customers: asset managers, housing companies, banks. Our customer base, our data, our credibility - that's valuable capital for the next step. Investment, credit, and asset management decisions in real estate are still made in Excel, case by case. We're now building the AI analyst that takes this work off people's hands - working directly on the customer's own data, scalable without adding headcount. We're well-funded, and we're bringing AI into real estate.

Your Mission

As a Data Scientist at Predium, you will help develop and improve the data-driven models behind our platform. You will use statistics, machine learning, and numerical methods to solve well-defined problems related to buildings, energy performance, and real-estate decarbonization.

Working closely with our engineering and product team, you will turn real-world data into reliable analytical, simulation, and machine-learning models that identify optimization opportunities for more sustainable buildings and help customers make informed investment decisions.

What you'll own

Develop and improve analytical, machine-learning, and simulation models to address business problems in the real-estate and energy domain.

Build and improve data extraction pipelines for structured and unstructured sources, evaluating extraction accuracy and reliability

Continuously explore and evaluate new data sources to improve model accuracy.

Assess data quality, identify gaps and evaluate model performance by validating assumptions and results against real-world data and feedback of domain experts.

Collaborate with data scientists, engineers, product managers, and other stakeholders to translate business needs into data-driven solutions.

What success looks like

You take ownership of well-defined analytical and modeling problems and independently deliver robust solutions.

Your models and analyses are reproducible, well-documented, and supported by appropriate validation.

You translate technical results into clear implications for the product, our customers, and the business.

You collaborate effectively across Data, Engineering and Product teams.

You actively seek feedback and use it to improve both your technical work and your way of working.

What it takes

A degree in data science, computer science, mathematics or a related field.

1–2 years of relevant hands-on experience, with programming, ideally in Python, through projects in areas such as physics-based modeling, machine learning, or data pipelines. TypeScript experience for product prototyping is a plus.

A structured, independent approach to problem-solving.

Curiosity about business needs and the ability to explain findings clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders.

Confident communication in English; German is a plus.

Bonus:

Initial experience with optimization methods, LLM-based data extraction, or uncertainty and sensitivity analysis.

Familiarity with real estate, building physics, or energy systems.

Experience with tools for physical simulation or energy modeling.

Why Predium?

Stage:
~40 people, well-funded, on the way to defining the category. Early enough that a lot still needs to be built. Yes, it's messy sometimes - that's the whole point. If you're looking for a job with a finished playbook, this isn't the right fit.

You're not cog #100 in some company. The models you build feed straight into our product and get used by real customers. Your contribution shows up directly, in revenue and in the product.

Ownership:
We don't manage your time, we measure your results. You get responsibility and freedom - and the expectation that you'll use both.

Competitive salary, bonus, and equity. We want you to share in the success you help create.

Office-first in Munich's Werksviertel, 4 days/week.

description: The NYC Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP) protects and enhances the daily economic lives of New Yorkers to create thriving communities. DCWP licenses nearly 45,000 businesses in more than 40 industries and enforces key consumer protection and workplace laws that apply to countless more. By supporting businesses through equitable enforcement and access to resources, DCWP protects the marketplace from predatory practices and strives to create a culture of compliance. DCWP empowers consumers and working families by providing the tools and resources they need to achieve financial health and work-life balance. DCWP also conducts research and advocates for public policy that furthers its work to support New York City’s communities. For more information about DCWP and its work, call 311 or visit DCWP at NYC Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP), sign up for its newsletter, or follow on its social media sites, X, Facebook, Instagram, and YouTube. Within DCWP, the Office of Financial Empowerment (OFE) focuses on initiatives that support New Yorkers and communities with low incomes in building wealth and improving their financial health. OFE is the first local government initiative in the country with the mission to educate, empower, and protect New Yorkers and neighborhoods with low incomes so they can build assets and make the most of their financial resources. OFE uses data and research, policy, partnerships, and convenings to advance its mission. Using this model, OFE is able to develop, offer, and advocate for innovative programs and products for all New Yorkers. To further its mission, OFE launched in January 2026, the Financial Literacy for Youth Initiative with the mission to connect NYC Public School students and their families to financial and consumer education programming to help them learn how to spend and save money so that they have a head start on being financially empowered adults. The City has committed funding to this initiative which will be overseen by DCWP, in collaboration with NYC Public Schools, to offer every student access to quality financial and consumer education by 2030. OFE designed the Financial Literacy for Youth Initiative with the goal to cultivate financially savvy youth by collaborating with educators, banking experts, and community partners to provide hands-on financial empowerment and consumer protection programming and services to youth and their families, while providing real-life professional development opportunities in school. This initiative launched in January 2026 with Financial Educators in 15 districts to lead the charge and deliver core programming, including 2Gen financial and consumer education workshops for both students and their families; on-site financial counseling; build school districts and schools capacity to integrate financial literacy inside and outside classrooms, and promotion of the Financial Education Resource Hub. OFE is seeking a Graduate Intern to join the Financial Counseling and Coaching team, with the primary responsibility of supporting the implementation of this new youth financial empowerment initiative. The Graduate Intern is, ideally, a graduate student studying instructional design and learning technology, and will work closely with the Senior Program Officer and Program Officer responsible for leading the implementation of the initiative, supporting the creation of the 2Gen financial education workshops for students and parents/caregivers and their alignment with NYS Education’s 2026 change to require personal finance education in all grade levels. The Graduate Intern will collaborate with other stakeholders, such as the DCWP External Affairs & Communications Division, NYC Public Schools, and OFE’s contracted providers, through the implementation of a youth initiative with the mission to cultivate financially savvy youth by providing hands-on financial empowerment and consumer protection services and real-life professional development opportunities in school. The Graduate Intern is an organized project manager with a strong commitment to supporting New Yorkers and communities with low incomes in building wealth and improving their financial health and a passion for financial education. The Graduate Intern will report to the Senior Program Officer for Financial Counseling and Coaching Programs. Responsibilities include, but are not limited to: • Assisting the Senior Program Officer with research on youth financial education and/or youth financial empowerment programs to inform the design and implementation of financial empowerment services focusing on youth and their families – including developing metrics, assessment tools, touchpoints for service integration, and operational strategy; • Supporting the Senior Program Officer in liaising with the DCWP External Affairs & Communications Division, NYC Public Schools, and MWBE vendors to coordinate and monitor the design and develop age-appropriate, engaging workshop curriculum materials on financial literacy topics (e.g., budgeting, savings, banking, credit, paying for college education, and consumer protection) and ensure that workshop content is culturally-relevant, inclusive, and accessible to diverse student populations. • Liaising and coordinating with the DCWP External Affairs and Communications Division and Division of Technology and Strategic Solutions, as well as MWBE vendors, to recommend instructional design models to guide the creation of digital and in-person learning experiences. • Under the supervision of the Senior Program Officer, and in coordination with the Policy and Research team, developing formative and summative assessment tools (e.g., pre/post surveys, quizzes, reflective prompts) to measure knowledge gains and shifts in attitudes or behaviors. • Working with OFE's Policy and Research team to understand and document the success of programs and assist with data analysis to inform iterative improvements to content and delivery methods and provide timely updates to OFE and DCWP leadership; • Maintaining clear documentation of curriculum frameworks, learning objectives, digital tools used, and impact metrics. • Providing general administrative assistance, including drafting, proofreading, and/or editing a range of materials, including but not limited to reports, program documents, and presentations. Support and contribute to broader team projects as needed as a Financial Counseling and Coaching team member.

description: ABOUT THE CAMPAIGN FINANCE BOARD The Campaign Finance Board is a nonpartisan, independent city agency that empowers New Yorkers to have a greater impact on their elections. Our mission is to make local democracy more open, transparent, and equitable by removing barriers to participation. We make it easier for New Yorkers to vote, meaningfully support candidates for city office, and run for office themselves. NYC Votes, our voter engagement initiative, meets people where they are to share trustworthy election information and help New Yorkers make a plan to vote. We publish the citywide Voter Guide, which delivers information about candidates directly to voters’ doors. Our public matching funds program ensures small contributions can make a big difference, allowing regular people to run for office by relying on the support of other regular people, not just wealthy donors and special interests. And we lift the veil on how candidates raise and spend money, increasing transparency and accountability in local government. We believe that when every New Yorker is empowered to participate meaningfully in elections, candidates will better reflect the communities they serve, elected leaders will be more accountable to the public, and New Yorkers will have a democracy they can truly trust. ABOUT THE UNIT Public Affairs Division The Public Affairs division engages New Yorkers, informs them about elections, and boosts their participation in the democratic process. We make election information accessible and relevant, increase engagement with underrepresented communities, and cultivate a team that reflects our core values of purpose, curiosity, creativity, and collaboration. The division includes, Marketing and Digital Communications, Community Engagement, Language Access, and Public Relations. Our division’s work includes publishing the citywide Voter Guide, running the official citywide Debates Program, and managing the voter engagement initiative, NYC Votes. Community Engagement Unit The Community Engagement unit works to build partnerships across the city to disseminate voting information, deliver accessible voter education, and conduct direct to voter outreach. Through relationships with community-based organizations as well as on-the-ground voter outreach, this team creates pathways for all New Yorkers to gain trustworthy and accessible information and education around voting and democracy. JOB DESCRIPTION The two Community Education Interns will report to the Youth Engagement Specialist and support civic education and engagement initiatives focused on a youth audience. Interns will help develop and deliver educational programming, support youth-focused events and partnerships, and engage young people in learning about voting and civic participation. Specifically, they will lead workshops on topics related to civic engagement and voter information for audiences of high school and college students both within internal youth programming and with external partners. The role will also support the Community Engagement team in building and maintaining strong internal systems to organize and track partnership development. This includes maintaining team databases, documenting outreach efforts, and supporting data entry. The responsibilities and tasks to be completed in this role include, but are not limited to: Community Education and Outreach - Support the development and delivery of educational programming, both internal and external, for a youth audience. - Independently plan and facilitate NYC Votes workshops in a way that engages the audience. - Represent the CFB and NYC Votes at in-person and virtual events. - Register voters and provide non-partisan election information. - Provide administrative support, such as managing email communication, organizing documents, carrying out internal processes, keeping materials organized, etc. - Identify organizations that work in our priority neighborhoods and serve a youth audience. - Support efforts to build relationships with key stakeholders, such as agencies, community-based organizations, schools, and college campuses. - Willingness to learn about best practices for engaging with priority communities. - Support the development and delivery of educational programming, both internal and external, for a youth audience; this includes leading lesson plans for youth ambassadors, leading workshops with external partners, and supporting curriculum development. - Support data entry efforts, including managing and digitizing physical documents, adding information to appropriate digital folders, and helping manage Excel sheets, etc. ESSENTIAL KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, ABILITIES & OTHER BEHAVIORS (KSAOs) We're seeking individuals eager to make an impact, even if they don't tick every box on our job description. description: The New York City Department of Investigation (DOI) is one of the oldest law enforcement agencies in the country; its mission is to combat municipal corruption. DOI serves the people of New York City by acting as an independent and nonpartisan watchdog for New York City government, City agencies, and City employees, vendors with City contracts, individuals and entities that receive City funds. The Deputy Commissioner/Chief Compliance and Equal Employment Opportunity Officer will report to the Commissioner and have dotted-line reporting obligations to the DOI General Counsel and Deputy Commissioner/Chief of Investigations, as necessary depending on the work involved. As DOI’s Chief Compliance Officer, the candidate will be responsible for agency risk mitigation; development and implementation of appropriate internal controls, including policies and procedures intended to ensure compliance with applicable legal and regulatory obligations; training and educating staff on compliance-related obligations; and management of internal complaints and investigations. The role includes, but is not limited to, the following tasks: • Manage the development, review, revision and implementation of agency policies, including those related to investigations and operations, such as the Code of Conduct, the Employee Manual, and Operational and Investigative Division policies, to ensure compliance with legal and regulatory requirements. • Provide guidance and recommendations on operational matters involving compliance, ethics, internal controls, and enterprise risk management. • Oversee and/or collaborate on internal and external audits, including forfeiture spending audits, the Executive Order No. 86 audit, eJustice audits, and any other audits that may arise or be needed. • Monitor and oversee the agency’s compliance with statutory, regulatory, and other reporting requirements. • Conduct internal investigations involving allegations of misconduct or violations of DOI policy or other compliance-related concerns. • Participate in the Investigator Training Program, including by leading training related to agency policies, procedures, compliance obligations, and ethical responsibilities. • Perform other executive-level responsibilities as directed by the Commissioner, including, but not limited to, collaborating with DOI’s Investigations Division, Operations Division, and General Counsel’s Office to interpret and apply laws, rules, regulations, and best practices to agency operations. As DOI’s Equal Employment Opportunity (“EEO”) Officer, the candidate will be responsible for promoting an inclusive and respectful work environment that is free from discrimination and harassment, consistent with the City of New York EEO Policy. The role includes, but is not limited to, the following tasks: • Serve as a leader in developing and implementing agency policies and practices that are consistent with the City’s EEO Policy and the agency’s goals of creating a diverse and inclusive workforce. • Conduct impartial investigations into discrimination, harassment, retaliation, and other violations of applicable EEO laws and City policy. • Provide training and advice to agency staff on EEO-related best practices, monitor agency compliance with mandatory EEO training requirements, and coordinate with agency stakeholders to ensure timely completion of required trainings. • Review and make determinations as to Reasonable Accommodation requests and, as appropriate, engage in the interactive process with employees and management concerning such requests. • Prepare and submit the City's Annual EEO Plan and other required citywide reports. • Monitor and review employment practices, including recruitment, hiring, promotions, transfers, and separations, to identify potential barriers to equal employment opportunity and ensure compliance with applicable laws and City policy. • Analyze workforce data and employment trends and recommend strategies to promote equal employment opportunity. • Serve as the agency liaison with Department of Citywide Administrative Services, the Equal Employment Practices Commission, the NYC Commission on Human Rights, and other oversight agencies on EEO-related matters. • Maintain confidential investigative files, records, and documentation in accordance with applicable policies and legal requirements. • Perform other related duties as assigned. description:
Accurx is solving healthcare productivity for the NHS
For decades, the NHS has struggled with fragmented systems that make simple tasks feel impossible. At Accurx, we’re changing that by building a single, system-wide platform that helps every patient get gold-standard, efficient, and joined-up care.
What started as a way for GPs to text a patient, has now evolved into an all-in-one digital toolkit used by 98% of GP practices and 68% (and growing!) of NHS Trusts.
Our platform now powers

Total Triage

to manage patient demand, and

Self-Book

that lets patients schedule their own appointments in seconds. We’ve automated routine care with

Patient Questionnaires
for long-term conditions, while

Accumail
finally allows staff-to-staff communication to happen instantly across different care settings. We’re now pushing the boundaries of the consultation itself with

Accurx Scribe
, our AI-powered note-taker that drafts medical notes in real-time.
We’re not just shipping features. We’re giving clinicians their time back and ensuring every patient journey is as smooth as it should be.
How you'll empower our tech and product leadership
You be a strategic partner and a vital force multiplier for our Chief Product Officer, Tom (CPrO) and incoming Chief Technology Officer (CTO). By anticipating their needs, shaping their organisational engagement, and prioritising their diaries against company objectives, you will help turn their strategic vision into real momentum across the Product & Technology teams.
Owning the operating rhythm:
You will proactively manage the executives' time and diaries, utilising your knowledge of Product Development Lifecycles and Engineering to effectively balance urgent requests with important strategic priorities.
Driving strategic communications:
You will draft, shape, and constructively challenge key messaging from the executives, ensuring communications are clear, consistent, and land successfully with various audiences.
Preparing with a point of view:
You will go beyond basic preparation by synthesising information, highlighting crucial details, and recommending decisions ahead of key meetings and board sessions.
Being the ear to the ground:
You will stay attuned to team sentiment and blockers across Product & Technology, bringing insights to the executives early and advising on the best response.
Fostering an AI-native culture:
You will partner with the executives and other Executive Assistants to design impactful cultural moments, such as hackathons and Town Hall meetings, ensuring momentum continues long after the events conclude.
Running the Product & Tech engine:
You will oversee logistics for the Product & Tech Leadership forum, manage fast-changing schedules, and monitor asynchronous Slack conversations to highlight matters needing executive attention.
Delivering impactful projects and events:
You will own and run projects on behalf of the executives from planning to delivery, while also managing the logistics for internal and external events, offsites, and team socials.

You have previously supported Product, Tech, or Engineering leaders within a B2B SaaS environment.

You excel at thinking multiple steps ahead, actioning potential next steps before the executives have even considered them.

You are a critical thinker who has the ability to challenge executives on their priorities, messaging, or plans to keep them focused on what matters.

You are confident leveraging AI tools, effective prompting, and automation to redefine how you work and find smarter ways to execute.

You have excellent time-management skills, meticulous attention to detail, and a proven track record managing fast-changing schedules and team events under tight deadlines.

THE AGENCY The Department of City Planning (DCP) plans for the future of New York City, working to create thriving and dynamic neighborhoods with access to housing and jobs, resilient infrastructure, and a vibrant public realm. The Department engages communities to develop inclusive plans, expand housing access and economic opportunity, and plans for long-term sustainability. DCP supports the City Planning Commission in its annual review of hundreds of land use applications. The Department also advises on citywide strategic and capital planning, analyzes data, conducts policy analysis, and creates open data and civic engagement tools. The Department of City Planning offers staff meaningful opportunities to help shape the future of New York City and address some of its most pressing challenges. The Department values public service, collaboration, and creativity, and supports professional development. Learn more about DCP at www.nyc.gov/planning. THE DIVISION Established to carry out the functions outlined in the SPEED Report, the Sprint Team is a new, dedicated project management team established to advance the Mamdani Administration's mandate to deliver affordable housing faster through streamlining the review of land use applications to reduce DCP pre-certification timelines for eligible projects from approximately two years to six months. The team will focus specifically on moving applications quickly, predictably, and transparently into public review while preserving the integrity of technical, zoning, and public review requirements. The land use application is the building block upon which the public discussion about the future of our city rests. The Division is responsible for the timely review of applications to ensure that decision-makers have the information necessary to make informed decisions about their communities. Working closely with DCP borough offices, the Technical Review Division, Environmental Assessment and Review, Pipeline and Commission Operations, Counsel, Capital Planning and Support, Strategic Planning, and the Mayor’s Office, the Sprint Team will identify eligible projects, establish clear review pathways, resolve critical path issues, track milestones, maintain high-quality data in DCP’s Zoning Applications Portal and related systems, and ensure that applicants and reviewers have clear expectations and guidance. The Sprint Team's primary responsibility is the direct management and review of complex land use applications progressing through pre-certification. Staff within the division will serve as lead project managers responsible for driving projects through the establishment of interdivisional guidance, identifying and escalating risks to schedule, coordinating guidance and comments to applicants and the City Planning Commission, maintaining accountability to milestone commitments, ensuring that applicants receive timely and actionable direction throughout the process, and providing transparency to the pre-certification pipeline through accurate reporting in DCP’s Zoning Application Portal. The Sprint Team will operate in a highly deadline-driven environment requiring strong judgment, collaboration, technical and planning knowledge, focus on creating and maintaining agency best practices, and a public service dedication. This work will directly support the City's housing production goals by leading a solutions-focused team to reduce avoidable delays while balancing the needs to provide thoughtful and accurate guidance on technical and zoning requirements and public review recommendations and strengthening DCP’s accountability to support the city’s goals for affordable housing production. THE ROLE The Deputy Director of the Sprint Team will assist in overseeing daily project management operations and supervise Team Leaders and project managers responsible for advancing eligible housing and land use applications through pre-certification review. The Deputy Director will coordinate directly with borough offices, other DCP divisions, applicants, and other stakeholders and monitor project statuses, resolve bottlenecks, and maintain accountability to established review timelines and schedules in close consultation with the Director. The Deputy Director will support prioritization and workflow management, staff supervision, milestone tracking, escalation coordination, quality control for application review, and implementation of operational procedures. The position will also assist with the development of reporting tools, performance metrics, staff training, and process improvement initiatives intended to improve review efficiency, communication, and transparency throughout the application review period. DCP leaders are responsible for setting the tone and ensuring everyone works together towards a common goal, which includes, but is not limited to, developing staff and teams and advancing division and agency work plans. 🎤 Founders Associate - a letter from the person you'd work with
Most job ads are written by no one, for everyone. I want to do this differently.
I'm
Marius
, Chief of Staff at voize. This role reports to me, and whoever takes it will work more closely with me than anyone else in the company. So instead of a template, here's what this job is, how I work, and how you can decide whether you'd want to work with me.
💡 What this job actually is
voize is growing fast, and fast-growing companies produce a specific kind of work: topics that matter but belong to no one. A new market needs operational groundwork. An org-wide process needs to be built. A decision needs a sharp analysis behind it. We're building a CEO Office to own exactly this work. You'd be its first hire.
I’ll be honest about the range. One week you’re working on a question that I and the rest of the management team will decide the company’s direction on. The next you're doing operational groundwork nobody will ever applaud. Both matter equally, it's the nature of building an early-stage company. If you need every task to feel glamorous, stop reading here. If "done" is your favorite word, keep going.
To make it concrete, your first months could look like this: you own the operational groundwork for one of our new markets end-to-end - research, vendor and partner setup, local operations - until things simply run. And you build one company-wide process from scratch, for example how cross-functional projects get scoped, prioritized, and tracked, and roll it out across the org. Different altitude, same job: you drive it to done.
🚀 How I work
I give trust and autonomy by default. The way I see my job as a manager: set goals you can actually reach, give you the resources to get there, unblock you when you're stuck, teach you what I know - and then get out of the way. I care about outcomes, not hours.
The flip side: you'll get a lot of freedom and little oversight. That's a gift if you work autonomously, and a problem if you don't. Autonomy doesn't mean silence, though. I expect you to ask for help early, not after something has quietly derailed.
I'm very opinionated and direct. You'll always know where you stand with me, and I expect the same back - including telling me when you think I'm wrong.
🎯 What I look for
Your background matters less than your pattern. You might come from consulting, VC, a startup, or something you built yourself. What I care about is this: you take ownership before anyone assigns it. You can be dropped into a topic you know nothing about and produce clarity within days. You hold a high bar for your own work without anyone checking. You ask a sharp question early instead of defending a wrong assumption late. And pace gives you energy instead of draining it.
If you read that and felt recognized rather than impressed - good sign.
🌱 Why voize
The care crisis is one of the most existential problems we face: fewer and fewer people caring for more and more of us. We build something that genuinely helps - over 200,000 caregivers use voize to win back time for people instead of paperwork. Purpose usually comes at the price of ambition. Not here. We combine real impact with high ambition and high speed, and that combination is rare. We raised a $50m Series A from leading investors like Balderton and HV end of last year and there is a lot ahead of us.
🤝 The deal
This job will be intense, and it will be fun. You'll get more exposure in your first year than most roles offer in five - to the CEO, me, the rest of the management team, and every part of the company. I'll invest in your growth personally. And the role isn't fixed: you'll shape it into what you want it to become.
If you read this and think this is for you, please apply no matter who you are or what background you have! I want to meet you 🫶
Marius

description:
IXPLAIN

Kaiserslautern, Germany (DFKI) | On-site / Hybrid | Co-Founder / Equity | Deep Tech / Explainable AI

About iXplain

iXplain is an AI platform for time series analysis that doesn't just detect what is happening in sensor data, but explains why. It combines state-of-the-art machine learning (classification, forecasting, regression, anomaly detection) with Explainable AI and a neuro-symbolic rule engine to turn raw industrial signals into clear, actionable recommendations, already demonstrated in water quality monitoring, energy grids and automotive production.

**The opportunity

**iXplain grew out of DFKI (German Research Center for Artificial Intelligence) and has a functional demonstrator, shown at Hannover Messe 2025, with live discussions underway in the water and manufacturing sectors. The technology is proven; the company is not yet founded. We are looking for a CEO / Business co-founder to turn a validated research demonstrator into a company, own the commercial relationship with our first industrial partners, and build the business around technology our 3-person research team has already built.

Tasks

What you will own

Company build-up

- Lead the incorporation of iXplain as a company and define its go-to-market strategy and business model.

- Own fundraising strategy and investor relations for the seed stage.

Commercial validation

- Validate iXplain with real industrial partners in water, energy and automotive/manufacturing, turning early discussions (post-Hannover Messe 2025) into paying pilots.

- Define how iXplain integrates into customers' existing workflows and systems.

Business leadership

- Build the commercial organization, pricing and sales process from scratch alongside the technical co-founders (Dr. Dominique Mercier, CTO; Dr. Tobias Wirth, Advisor).

- Represent iXplain to investors, partners and industrial customers as CEO.

Requirements

What you bring

Core experience

- Entrepreneurial / business leadership experience, ideally as a founder or in early-stage B2B SaaS or industrial-tech commercialization.

- Track record in business development and closing deals with industrial or enterprise customers.

- Comfortable operating without a playbook, pre-product-market-fit.

Especially valuable

- Domain expertise in water, energy, or automotive/manufacturing industries.

- Experience fundraising from VCs or deep-tech grants (e.g., EXIST, German public funding).

- Ability to speak the language of both data-science researchers and industrial buyers.

Benefits

Why join iXplain

- Own the CEO seat of a deep-tech AI company with a working, demonstrated product, not a slide deck.

- Backed by DFKI's research and IP in Explainable AI and neuro-symbolic reasoning.

- Equity-based co-founder role with real influence on strategy, hiring and company direction from day one.

iXplain welcomes co-founder candidates regardless of gender, age, ethnic origin, religion or belief, disability, sexual identity, or any other characteristic. This is a search for the right partner to build the company with, not a conventional hire.

description:
🌍 About Zauber
After co-founding and scaling
Forto
to over $600M in funding, I took a step back to reflect on what’s still broken in global logistics. The answer was clear: it’s still a human-first, spreadsheet-heavy industry, full of repetitive processes and broken system interoperability.
With the rise of AI agents, we now have the tools to rethink that from the ground up. Zauber builds autonomous agents for the global logistics industry, AI workers that handle operational tasks, talk to systems and humans alike, and get better every day.
🚢 We're already live with global logistics leaders in Europe and Asia
💰 Backed by P9 - one of Europe's top early-stage funds
📈 Growing fast and hiring exceptional talent to join early
Now we are looking for an exceptional Founder's Associate Intern helping us grow and bring Zauber to the next stage.
🧠 What You'll Do
You'll be a core part of a small and fast-moving team. This is a hands-on, high-ownership role where you will help us scale both product and company operations while learning directly from experienced operators and founders along the way.
• Build and manage internal systems like our website and tooling
• Lead recruiting efforts and support onboarding of new team members
• Support go-to-market initiatives and help bring our agents to customers
• Identify and secure grant and non-dilutive funding opportunities
• Tackle whatever challenge moves the company forward
👤 You Might Be a Fit If You...
• Enjoy solving a wide range of problems in dynamic environments
• Are curious about startups, AI, and how companies are built
• Take full ownership and pride in execution
• Are able to switch between big-picture thinking and detailed execution
• Aspire to build something meaningful and potentially start your own company
🛠 What You Bring
• Experience in generalist roles, ideally in early-stage or high-agency environments
• A somewhat technical background or strong intuition for AI and software
• Strong communication skills in both German and English
• High integrity, strong work ethic, and a sense of urgency
📍 Location & Logistics
• Berlin office preferred
• Start: Q4 2026
• Compensation: 2,400€ per month
💼 What We Offer
• A role with real responsibility from day one
• A close-knit team that values action, clarity, and customer impact
• Access to experienced operators and strong mentorship
• The chance to shape one of Europe’s most ambitious AI startups
🚀 Why Now
We’re not a demo company. We’re in production with real customers, in one of the world’s most critical and complex industries. Demand is not our bottleneck, execution is. Logistics remains largely untouched by intelligent automation — legacy systems, manual processes, and fragmented workflows make it one of the most fertile grounds for AI transformation.
This is your opportunity to learn company building by doing. You will not be a passive observer but an active driver of what gets built and how we grow.
We envision a world where every shipment is proactively managed by intelligent agents. Where operators have superhuman capabilities at their fingertips and trade never stalls.
🇪🇺 Building from Europe
What drives us personally is the belief that Europe’s long-term prosperity and sovereignty depend on a strong economic engine. We need more AI product-first European global champions on the world stage.
Our mission is to build one of the biggest automation companies in the world - from Europe. While our HQ will be in Europe, we will relentlessly benchmark ourselves with the best globally and sell internationally from the beginning.

Founders Associate - Engagement Innovation
to help us make JustPlay app ecosystem dramatically more fun, exciting and engaging.
You'll work directly with our founders across every product team, constantly looking for ideas that make users want to click, play, win, explore and come back.
We're not looking for someone to manage roadmaps or introduce more product processes. We're looking for someone with exceptional consumer instincts, extremely high agency and an obsession with the mechanics behind the world's most engaging B2C products.
You should be the kind of person who opens an app like TikTok, Temu, MONOPOLY GO!, Duolingo or Whatnot and immediately starts dissecting why it works and how those ideas could be applied somewhere completely different.
Some of your ideas may become major features. Others might be a different CTA, a more exciting reward reveal, a new event, better framing of a prize, or an experiment we can ship next week.
We care much more about the impact of an idea than its complexity.

Work directly with the founders as a thinking partner on what makes JustPlay exciting to play
Embed across product teams to find opportunities — not to run them
Maintain a constant flow of ideas, from single-line copy changes to entirely new mechanics
Tear down the world's most engaging consumer apps and translate what works there into what could work here
Turn ideas into things people can act on: a sharp one-pager, a mock, a test plan — whatever gets it moving fastest
Push ideas through to launch by making yourself useful to the teams shipping them
Measure what happens, tell the truth about it, and scale or kill accordingly
Build our collective instinct for engagement, so the whole company gets better at this over time

Exceptional consumer instincts: you can tell why something is fun or addictive, not just that it is
Extremely high agency: you find the problem, propose the answer, and chase it until it's live, without being assigned it

description:
FAMILY FLOW

Saarbrücken / Homburg, Saarland, Germany | Remote | Fulltime | Digital Health (DiGA)

About Family Flow

Family Flow is a scientifically grounded, trauma-sensitive parenting app that helps parents with their own history of adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) manage the moment between a trigger and their reaction to their child — building a personalized 'Flow Plan' (trigger → warning signs → pause → skill → parenting strategy) instead of another generic parenting app.

The opportunity

The concept is built on more than 20 years of clinical and scientific work on child maltreatment led by Prof. Dr. med. Eva Möhler, Chair of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry at Saarland University, alongside DFKI researchers Patrick Gebhard and Jan Alexandersson. The idea and clinical content are finalized — what's missing is the team and funding to build and launch the app. We are looking for a CEO / Business co-founder (fundraising, tech and operations) to turn a validated clinical concept into a real product.

Tasks

What you will own

Company build-up & fundraising

- Lead incorporation of Family Flow and raise the funding needed for app development (German, French and English versions).

- Own the path to the German DiGA directory (digital health app reimbursement) and the parallel free-market / B2C launch.

Product & delivery

- Translate the finalized clinical concept and psychotherapeutic material into a software roadmap, in partnership with a tech/development team or subcontractor (e.g. potential partnerships with Pioneo, Pfeffermind or Charamel).

- Own day-to-day operations, as the current interdisciplinary team (DFKI + Child and Adolescent Psychiatry) is part-time only.

Go-to-market

- Build the launch plan for Germany and France, then wider Europe, including social-media-led B2C acquisition alongside the DiGA pathway.

Requirements

What you bring

Core experience

- Fundraising experience (grants and/or investors) and comfort building a company from an academic/clinical concept.

- Hands-on operations and project management skills; willingness to work full-time (the current founding team is part-time).

Especially valuable

- Experience with the digital health / DiGA regulatory pathway in Germany.

- Software/product background, or strong ability to manage external development partners.

- Interest in child psychiatry, trauma-informed care or parenting technology.

Benefits

Why join Family Flow

- A clinically validated concept backed by 20+ years of research and a published evidence base, not an unproven idea.

- Direct partnership with a University Professor and Chair of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry at Saarland University.

- Address a problem estimated to cost society €20 billion in Germany alone (Deutsche Traumafolgekostenstudie), with a clear DiGA reimbursement path.

Family Flow welcomes co-founder candidates regardless of gender, age, ethnic origin, religion or belief, disability, sexual identity, or any other characteristic. This is a search for the right partner to build the company with, not a conventional hire.

About the Company

Affinidi
is a technology company dedicated to changing data ownership for good. We empower businesses and individuals with control and ownership of their data, with a comprehensive approach to managing their holistic identity – accounting for all aspects of their digital footprint while ensuring privacy and security.

Affinidi’s technology enables users to benefit from decentralised digital identity solutions. We believe that everyone has the right to own and control their data, and we are committed to creating a trusted digital credentials ecosystem that empowers businesses and individuals to securely exchange data and services across borders and industries.

We’re looking for a Senior Product Manager (Technical) who wants to help define how trust is built into the next generation of AI systems. At Affinidi, we’re building the Trust Fabric product suite to give AI agents verifiable identity, policy guardrails, and real-time observability, so organisations can move from promising proofs of concept to secure, governed production deployments with confidence.

This is a role for builders. You’ll work side by side with engineering to turn ambitious ideas into real, high-impact products, fast, iteratively, and with strong product judgment. You’ll take on complex, ambiguous challenges that don’t come with a playbook, bring structure to what matters, and help the team move with clarity, speed, and conviction. You’ll also collaborate with deeply engaged teams and senior leaders in an environment that expects high standards, values ownership, and gives you the chance to shape meaningful products from the ground up.

If you like combining technical depth, product thinking, and execution, you’ll fit right in.

What you’ll be doing

Shape and deliver solutions
:
Partner closely with engineers to define and refine solutions early, helping move ideas from concept to production in practical, incremental steps while staying close enough to implementation to understand trade-offs and guide decisions.

Drive focused, outcome-oriented delivery:

Balance user needs, market context, and execution speed while focusing on getting working solutions into users’ hands for validation, then iterate based on feedback and measurable outcomes.

Work through ambiguity
:

Take ownership of areas where requirements are not fully defined, structure problems into clear, actionable paths forward, and maintain momentum even as direction continues to evolve.

Own product direction:

Contribute to product strategy and roadmap definition, align short-term priorities with longer-term platform thinking, and make thoughtful trade-offs that support both delivery and scalability.

Collaborate across stakeholders
:
Work across engineering, design, and go-to-market teams, engage effectively with senior and executive stakeholders, and bring alignment and clarity in environments with diverse perspectives.

Be developer-obsessed
:

Understand developer workflows and key pain points, and help improve integration, usability, and the overall product experience.

What we’re looking for

Core experience
:
You bring 5+ years of experience in Technical Product Management, a strong technical background that lets you engage deeply with engineering topics, hands-on experience working with APIs, systems, and integrations, and a proven track record of delivering products in close collaboration with engineering teams.

Technical depth
:
You are comfortable understanding how systems are designed and operate in practice, able to engage in technical discussions, challenge assumptions, and evaluate trade-offs, and willing to go into detail when needed by reviewing flows, investigating issues, or clarifying implementation approaches.

Mindset
:
You take ownership from problem to outcome, are comfortable working with ambiguity and evolving priorities, combine structured thinking with a bias toward action, and can move between big-picture strategy and practical execution.

Collaboration & communication
:
You communicate effectively across technical and non-technical audiences, are comfortable working with experienced, highly engaged stakeholders, and know how to build alignment and drive decisions forward.

Nice to have
:
It’s a plus if you have had exposure to identity, distributed systems, or similar domains, and experience in fast-paced, product-led environments.

What you’ll get

A team that values ownership, quality, and speed

Close collaboration between product and engineering

Hybrid working model in Berlin + flexible hours

Unlimited vacation

Competitive compensation

A strong environment to learn, build, and have impact

Equal Opportunity

job_title: Director Venture Scaling - iF Momentum (all genders)
description:
Your mission
Breakthrough technologies can create entirely new industries and companies of global relevance – but only if scientific excellence is matched by exceptional execution, capital and commercial ambition. As Director Venture Scaling iF Momentum, your mission is to help build the next generation of DeepTech champions: companies with the potential to become category leaders, scale internationally and transform their industries. You will work side by side with exceptional founders, opening access to industry, capital and talent while developing iF Momentum into a leading European platform for scaling ambitious DeepTech ventures.
Take ownership of iF Momentum and its portfolio of highly ambitious DeepTech ventures, helping founders build companies with the potential to become global category leaders while ensuring outstanding program quality, team performance, budget discipline and measurable impact.
Identify venture-scale opportunities and challenge founders on the fundamental choices that determine scale: market ambition, positioning, value propositions, business models and commercial strategies and the path towards building a globally competitive company.
Turn technological advantage into commercial momentum by helping ventures move from first market validation towards repeatable customer demand, scalable go-to-market models and international growth.
Drive commercial and industry scale-up by helping startups develop customer use cases, industrial pilots, venture-client collaborations, licensing models and strategic partnerships – and turn early validation into repeatable commercial traction.
Build the financing pathway required for scale – from the next institutional funding round to the capital required for industrialisation and international growth – by challenging financial models, cap tables, equity stories, funding strategies, investor materials and data rooms.
Establish clear milestones and priorities for each venture, continuously challenge whether they are on the fastest credible path towards commercial scale, and deploy program resources where they can create the greatest enterprise value and impact.
Lead and develop a multidisciplinary venture-building team and coordinate closely with colleagues across the wider Impossible Founders platform.
Build and activate a high-calibre network of founders, investors, corporates, and experts that can materially accelerate the growth of iF Momentum ventures.
Secure new sponsorships, strategic partnerships and commercial opportunities, and develop scalable business models and future revenue streams for iF Momentum.
Your profile
What matters most to us
You know what separates a promising technology from a venture-scale company and have the judgement to identify opportunities with the potential to build significant, globally competitive businesses.
You bring substantial professional experience from venture capital, entrepreneurship, venture building, transaction or strategy advisory, venture building, or a fast-growing technology company – ideally with direct exposure to building, financing or scaling ambitious technology ventures.
You fully understand the specific challenges of DeepTech commercialisation and can bridge the worlds of science, technology, industry and capital.
You have worked closely with ambitious founders through critical stages of company building – ideally including commercial scale-up, institutional fundraising, international expansion or the creation of a new market category.
You are confident working with business plans, financial models, cap tables, market and competitive analyses, due diligence materials and investor narratives.
You have successfully supported startups turn commercial strategy into traction – developing customers, industry partnerships, pilots and go-to-market models that can ultimately scale beyond individual projects.
You combine strategic judgement with a hands-on mindset and are comfortable challenging founders on ambition, priorities, milestones and difficult decisions.
You can already bring in an established network of investors, industry partners, and senior operators and know how to activate it when it can materially accelerate a venture.
You have experience leading teams, projects or portfolios and know how to create clear responsibilities, high quality standards and an effective delivery culture.
You communicate clearly and credibly with founders, executives, investors, scientists and external partners in an international environment.
You are fluent in English; German language skills are highly desirable.
Additionally, it would be a plus if you bring
Practical exposure to patents, intellectual property strategies, licensing processes or technology transfer.
Experience with industrial pilots, venture-client models, joint development agreements or other forms of startup–industry collaboration, or experience scaling your own startup.
Exposure to public grants, non-dilutive funding or blended financing strategies.
Why us?
At Impossible Founders, the people behind the impossible are the most important catalyst. That's why we do everything we can to create a collaborative working environment:
Responsibility & autonomy:
You take on real responsibility from day one and have the freedom to actively shape your role and the company. Output counts, and you are given the freedom you need to do your job in the best possible way.
Flexible & family-friendly working
: We offer a high degree of flexibility through our hybrid work setup. Mondays are our shared office day, while on other days you can choose whether to work remotely or from the office — depending on what works best for your role, team, and personal circumstances.
Meaningful mission & impact:
You will work on projects that address real challenges in AI, climate tech, and beyond. You will achieve impact and visibility by working closely with founders, researchers, and leading partners.
Collaborative culture & diversity:
We cultivate a collaborative culture - practical, ego-free, and driven by shared responsibility. Our team is characterized by diversity and openness. The company language is English so that everyone feels welcome.
Attractive working conditions:
30 days of vacation

International team and English as company language
Central office in a prime location
Choice of your own hardware

The Team

Forward Deployed Engineering owns how Tavily shows up technically in the field. The team sits at the intersection of customers, Product, Engineering, Sales, Partnerships, and Customer Success.

The Enterprise FDE motion focuses on Tavily’s highest-value customers and strategic enterprise opportunities — from technical discovery and solution design through proof of concept, production rollout, adoption, and expansion.

The role

This is a full-time, on-site role based in our New York office.

As a Forward Deployed Engineer, Enterprise, you’ll work directly with Tavily’s largest and most strategic customers to design, prototype, and deploy production-grade AI systems powered by Tavily’s API. You’ll own the technical relationship across the customer lifecycle, helping enterprise teams move from early use case exploration to deployed, scalable agentic applications.

You’ll be deeply hands-on: building RAG pipelines, agent workflows, evaluation loops, reference architectures, and custom integrations alongside customer teams. You’ll also serve as a critical bridge between the field and our Product and Engineering teams, translating enterprise needs into roadmap signal.

Your responsibilities will include:

Work directly with enterprise customers to understand their AI use cases, technical architecture, success criteria, and deployment requirements.

Lead technical discovery and solution design during pre-sales and expansion conversations.

Scope, build, and deliver proofs of concept that demonstrate clear business and technical value.

Design and implement production-ready integrations using Tavily’s API, including RAG pipelines, agent workflows, internal tools, and industry-specific GenAI applications.

Partner with customer engineering, data, product, and AI teams to move use cases from prototype to production.

Monitor customer API usage patterns and recommend improvements to increase reliability, latency, coverage, and overall value.

Translate recurring customer needs, blockers, and technical patterns into clear product and roadmap input.

Create reusable enterprise assets, including reference architectures, integration templates, deployment guides, demo environments, and technical documentation.

Represent Tavily in customer architecture reviews, executive technical conversations, implementation check-ins, and post-deployment reviews.

Partner closely with Sales, Customer Success, Product, and Engineering to drive adoption, retention, and expansion across strategic accounts.

We expect you to have:

5+ years of software engineering experience, ideally in a customer-facing technical role such as Forward Deployed Engineer, Solutions Architect, Solutions Engineer, Sales Engineer, or Technical Consultant.

Strong hands-on engineering ability, especially with Python, APIs, backend systems, and production software development.

Experience building with LLMs, Retrieval-Augmented Generation, agent architectures, context engineering, and modern AI application stacks.

Experience working with enterprise customers, including technical discovery, POCs, solution design, stakeholder management, and production rollout.

Strong understanding of how enterprises evaluate, deploy, secure, and scale AI systems.

Ability to communicate clearly with both technical and executive stakeholders, including engineering leaders, product teams, AI teams, and technical decision-makers.

High autonomy, strong ownership, and comfort operating in a fast-moving startup environment.

Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to turn complex technical concepts into clear recommendations.

Based in New York City, or willing to relocate.

It will be an added bonus if you have:

Experience working with major agent or LLM orchestration frameworks such as LangChain, LlamaIndex, LangGraph, OpenAI Agents SDK, or CrewAI.

Experience with vector databases such as Pinecone, Weaviate, pgvector, Qdrant, or similar systems.

Experience with enterprise AI use cases in financial services, legal, consulting, enterprise SaaS, sales, marketing, or internal knowledge management.

Track record helping large customers move from POC to production.

Experience building internal tools, technical playbooks, demos, or reusable customer-facing assets.

Prior experience at a high-growth AI infrastructure, developer tools, or enterprise SaaS company.

description:
At Upvest, we are on a
mission to make investing as easy as spending money
. Upvest empowers businesses to offer a wide range of investment products and the best experience in the field of capital market investment and retirement planning. Upvest’s Investment API is easy to integrate so that fintechs and financial institutions can save resources and fully focus on their core business.
We are proud to partner with Europe’s leading Fintechs and financial institutions such as DKB, Revolut, N26 and Raisin. Founded in 2017 by Martin Kassing, Upvest now brings together over 270 talented professionals from more than 70 nationalities. Upvest is backed by €280M in total funding from world-class investors, including BlackRock, Tencent, Sapphire Ventures, and Bessemer Venture Partners, Earlybird, Notion Capital, and Motive. Our latest €105M funding round in March 2026 - led by Sapphire and Tencent - serves as a massive catalyst for our growth, allowing us to offer premier investment experience.
About the role:
The role is designed for law graduates who are pursuing a doctorate (Promotion) or preparing for the (Zweite) Juristische Prüfung and want hands-on in-house experience in a regulated investment firm alongside their academic work. You will work closely with our lawyers and take on increasing responsibility over time.
What you’ll do:
Support our Legal Team on domestic and international projects, in particular by reviewing and preparing first drafts of cooperation agreements with clients and partners.
Research legal questions raised by our Product, Project Management and Sales teams and prepare concise memos, with a focus on financial services regulation (e.g. WpIG, MiFID II, DORA).
Conduct initial legal reviews and risk assessments of vendor agreements and summarise the key points for the responsible lawyer.
Help develop and maintain our standard contracts, templates, playbooks and other key legal documents essential to operations.
Maintain and structure our contract inventory (contract management database) to ensure completeness, compliance and clear ownership.
Collaborate closely with the Legal Team to automate, operationalise and improve internal processes, including with AI-based legal tech tools.
Monitor regulatory developments relevant to Upvest (e.g. Bafin, ESMA, EU legislation) and prepare short briefings for the team.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Tide is hiring a VP of Engineering to lead the engineering organisation behind Ongoing Monitoring. You will report directly to the Chief Data and Technology Officer. Ongoing Monitoring protects our members by detecting fraud, financial crime and regulatory risk across every transaction Tide processes. The engineering, data science and platform capability behind it is one of the most technically demanding estates at Tide.

You will be accountable for the engineering strategy, organisation and execution across all Ongoing Monitoring value streams: real-time transaction monitoring for bank payments fraud, acquiring fraud, Anti Money Laundering, Counter Terrorist Financing, sanctions and prohibited activities monitoring, and the tooling our financial investigators depend on. Set the engineering strategy for Tide's fraud, financial crime and ongoing monitoring platforms

Lead engineering across backend, frontend, data science, ML engineering and analytics engineering, primarily based in Hyderabad with product leadership split between Hyderabad and London

Lead managers and senior engineers, and build the leadership bench underneath you

Work with multiple stakeholders across risk, operations, business, design, product and engineering

Own the Decision Engine and Decision Intelligence Platform as shared capabilities, unifying domestic and international payment flows

Own the model lifecycle end to end, from development through backtesting, shadow deployment and staged rollout to production performance monitoring

Scale agentic AI in regulated workflows, including migrating Ongoing Monitoring agents onto Tide's shared agentic infrastructure and holding the line on our agentic governance framework

Deliver measurable risk and efficiency outcomes: lower fraud losses, higher automated alert throughput, and a falling ongoing monitoring cost per member

Build the operating model that connects first line operations, second line risk and compliance, payments and acquiring engineering, KYX, AI Platforms and data science leadership behind one roadmap

Apply principles so we build once, deploy globally, and keep market-specific logic isolated

Experience leading engineering organisations in fraud, financial crime, risk or another real-time decisioning domain

Experience operating in a regulated environment, working with second line risk and compliance functions and with regulators

Strong judgement across organisation design, delivery, platform strategy, data architecture and technical quality

Ability to lead distributed teams across multiple markets and align several functions behind one roadmap, operating model and set of priorities

Experience deploying AI or agentic systems inside regulated workflows, with a clear view on governance, evaluation and human oversight would be a bonus

DeutschlandTicket via Spendit - Employer funded free, unlimited travel throughout Germany on all local public transport (not valid in ICE, IC/EC).

Volunteering & Development Days – Paid days annually for volunteering or personal growth.

Learning & Development – Annual budget for books, courses, coaching, and more.

WOO (Work Outside the Office) – Work from abroad for up to 90 days annually.

Home Office Setup – Contribution towards setting up your home office.

Laptop Ownership – Keep your old laptop and get a new one when it’s time for a replacement.

TIDEAN WAYS OF WORKING

flexible workplace
model that

supports both in-person and remote work to cater to the specific needs of our different teams.

While remote work is supported, we believe in the power of face-to-face interactions to foster team spirit and collaboration. Our offices are designed as hubs for innovation and team-building, where we encourage regular in-person gatherings to foster a strong sense of community.
